definition: A list of numbers in order, made by a rule, such as $4, 7, 10, 13, \ldots$
The rule that gets each term of a sequence from the term before it, such as "add $3$" or "divide by $2$".
A formula in $n$ that gives any term of a sequence from its position $n$; for $3n + 1$, the 10th term is $3 \times 10 + 1 = 31$.
A sequence that goes up or down by the same amount each time, such as $5, 9, 13, 17, \ldots$; its nth term looks like $dn + c$.
A sequence whose second differences (the gaps between the gaps) are all the same and not zero; its nth term has $n^2$ as the highest power, as in $n^2 + 1$.
A sequence whose third differences are all the same and not zero; its nth term has $n^3$ as the highest power, as in $n^3 + 2$.
A sequence where you multiply by the same number each time, such as $2, 6, 18, 54, \ldots$; its nth term is $a \times r^{n-1}$, where $a$ is the first term and $r$ the number you multiply by.
